messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher service reported elevated P99 latency and GPU OOMs in us-west-2-prod. auto-page -> #eng-oncall. severity: high :rotating_light:

matt_oncall: saw it, tailing logs now. which pool?

priya: batcher-v2 on p-gpu-pool-7. metrics: inflight batch size steadily increasing, KV cache memory growing, paging spikes to 90% on node-3.

devon: ugh, node-3 got 2x container restarts within 5m. cuda out-of-memory in logs: "CUDARuntimeError: out of memory when allocating 1.2GiB"

matt_oncall: ok triage plan: 1) throttle continuous-batcher globally to cap max_batch=8 2) evict large prefixes from KV cache 3) drain node-3 and restart runtime container 4) route critical customer traffic to fallback model in us-west-1. executing step 1 now.

matt_oncall: /ops set-config continuous-batcher max_batch 8 --scope=us-west-2

incident-bot: Command accepted: config updated. new max_batch=8.

alexa: sending short-circuit to routing: canary fallback model is rdx-small-v2 in us-west-1, will shift 20% of traffic for 5m.

customer-ops-bot: Alert: ~4.7k requests failed with 500s in last 10m; impact: some enterprise customers experiencing latency >10s. Escalation flag set.

priya: watching memory: KV cache dropped ~30% after throttle, but prefetch/growth loop still active on a couple pods.

devon: I see a deadlock pattern in batch-accumulator where queue depth never drains because long requests keep being re-batched. patch suggestion: short-circuit requests older than 1200ms.

matt_oncall: good catch. temporary mitigation: enable request-age cutoff = 1200ms on continuous-batcher. /ops set-config continuous-batcher max_age_ms 1200 --scope=us-west-2

incident-bot: Command accepted: max_age_ms=1200.

sre-ops: starting drain on node-3. kubectl cordon node-3 && kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m

alexa: restarting runtime containers on drained pods with debug flags: --kvcache-compact=1 --kv-prefetch=off

devon: rolling restart acknowledged. logs show one container crashing with kernel OOM before graceful exit. suspicion: container oom triggered host-level GPU memory pressure -> cuda error -> container backoff.

matt_oncall: manual step: add temporary job to restart any pod that shows CUD A OOM exit and annotate for postmortem.

priya: routing shift to fallback done. p99 latency for the affected route dropped from 9.8s -> 1.2s. errors dropping.

customer-ops-bot: Noted: customer ticket #C-1142 updated: "We saw spike in latency and 500s, root cause being runtime OOMs. Traffic routed to fallback; will monitor."

devon: pushing a small hotfix to prevent unbounded KV prefetch growth: limit-prefetch = 64 items; will deploy to canary (1 pod) in 2m.

matt_oncall: agree, do canary, monitor mem + paging. if stable -> rollout. also open a mitigation runbook item to disable continuous-batcher’s aggressive prefetch by default.

priya: canary pods report stable mem and no paging after hotfix. rolling rollout initiated across p-gpu-pool-7.

alexa: after roll, node-3 drain completed, uncordon. cluster GPU paging back to normal ~12%. no further container restarts in last 8m.

matt_oncall: customer impact summary for now: ~45 min window with elevated latency/500s for a subset of traffic in us-west-2. primary cause: continuous-batcher unbounded batch growth + KV prefetch leading to host GPU memory pressure -> CUDA OOM and container crashes -> node flaps. mitigation: throttle max_batch, set request-age cutoff, limit prefetch, drain/restart affected node, route traffic to fallback model.

devon: follow-ups (owners): 1) devon - permanent patch to prefetch limiter + tests (by EOD) 2) priya - add circuit-breaker in routing to detect and shift traffic faster (next 48h) 3) matt_oncall - postmortem and severity assessment (tomorrow) 4) sre-ops - add alert for KV cache growth anomaly (48h)

matt_oncall: I'll file incident ticket and link metrics/dashboards/log excerpts. temporary config changes will be reverted after postmortem-approved fixes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (manual) at 1768901542. Reason: sustained reduction in errors and stable memory metrics after mitigations. Post-incident PM requested.

matt_oncall: thanks everyone. leaving notes in #incidents and starting postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

alexa: +1, will follow up on routing playbook updates.

priya: adding reproduction steps to the postmortem: synthetic workload to trigger KV prefetch and batch buildup.

devon: adding unit/integration tests for batch accumulator and deadline timers.

customer-ops-bot: Customer notify: message queued for impacted accounts: "We've mitigated an infrastructure issue causing latency/500s. Root cause investigation in progress. We'll follow up with postmortem."
